problem: Saying v = L di/dt and i = C dv/dt are "straight lines through the origin" is right for the resistor's v–i graph but loose for L and C: the straight-line relation is between v and di/dt (or dv/dt), not between v and i. A student may think an inductor's v–i plot is a line.
fix: Resistors, ideal capacitors and ideal inductors are linear elements. For a resistor v = Ri is a straight line through the origin; for an inductor the linear relation is between v and di/dt, and for a capacitor between i and dv/dt. All three are linear relations with constant coefficients.

where: Section 2, worked-example derivation paragraph beginning "Why it works" in Section 1
problem: "Such a set has exactly one solution" is stated without a condition. A nodal or mesh system has exactly one solution only when the coefficient matrix is nonsingular; some circuits (certain dependent-source and ideal-source combinations) have no solution or many. The superposition argument does not need uniqueness.
fix: Such a set, when the circuit is well posed, has exactly one solution, and that solution is a linear combination of the right-hand sides.

problem: "Zeroing its gain deletes a real contribution" is confusing. Superposition switches off a source by making its value 0, not by touching the gain constant μ, g, r or β.
fix: Its value is set by a voltage or current elsewhere in the circuit, not fixed by itself. Setting its value to zero erases a contribution that really exists in the other runs and changes the equations, so the dependent source is kept and re-evaluated in every reduced circuit.

problem: The sentence "as long as the group runs and the single-source runs together cover every source exactly once" is hard to follow and makes it sound as if both group runs and single-source runs are needed.
fix: Three runs, one per source. Grouping is allowed instead: every source must be switched on in exactly one run and in no other. For three sources, one valid choice is a run with source 1 alone and a second run with sources 2 and 3 both on.
